channel_name: This Week in Startups · Jason Calacanis
video_title: Binance Hacked $6.3B Stolen, DoorDash Buys Instacart For $17B, Jake Newfield from Hermetiq, + More!
gist: Jason Calacanis and Lon Harris cover the Binance hack (~$6.3B affected, the largest crypto hack on record, reportedly via a compromised engineer's laptop, with Binance pledging to cover all losses and ~$3B frozen on-chain) and DoorDash's ~$17B cash-and-stock acquisition of Instacart at $65/share, which Calacanis expects to clear quickly under Trump-era antitrust and calls an overpay justified by DoorDash's 88x P/E stock. Launch accelerator winner Jake Newfield pitches Hermetiq, an AI build-engineering data layer for Bazel already paid $240K by a top AI lab; the rest is sponsor reads, an Annotated app bounty and a Patrick Stewart tribute.

insights.claim: Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, was hit by a complex attack affecting an estimated $6.3 billion, which the hosts call the largest crypto hack in recorded history.
insights.speaker: Lon Harris
insights.so_what: Centralized exchange custody risk is back in focus at unprecedented scale.
insights.quote: they were hit by a complex attack affecting an estimated $6.3 billion.

insights.claim: Binance says it will cover all losses with more than $6.3 billion of company funds and has suspended deposits and withdrawals; early investigation points to a compromised engineer's laptop enabling unauthorized withdrawals.
insights.speaker: Lon Harris
insights.so_what: Endpoint compromise of a single employee can breach exchange controls; the backstop limits contagion.
insights.quote: a compromised engineer's laptop may have allowed the attacker to submit unauthorized withdrawals.

insights.claim: Tether, Circle, Ripple and World Liberty Financial helped freeze affected assets, with about $3 billion frozen on-chain so far.
insights.speaker: Lon Harris
insights.so_what: Stablecoin issuers' freeze powers are now a key recovery tool in major hacks.

insights.claim: Calacanis credits CZ, who owns about 90% of privately held Binance and is worth roughly $110 billion, for backstopping losses that may be ~20% of his net worth, after CZ's 2023 guilty plea, four-month sentence and 2025 Trump pardon.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: Owner-funded backstops can preserve exchange franchises, but depend on one person's wealth.

insights.claim: Calacanis reiterates his 2021 advice not to keep money on Binance and urges spreading funds across multiple banks and custodians, citing the SVB lesson and $250,000 FDIC limits.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: Counterparty diversification is essential for founders and crypto holders alike.
insights.quote: I would not trust leaving your money in Binance. That sounds like the stupidest thing you could ever do.

insights.claim: Calacanis predicts corporate cybersecurity spending, now low single digits as a share of budgets, needs to double, and proposes an industry-wide month with no new feature releases devoted to patching.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: AI-era attacks could drive a step-up in security budgets benefiting cyber vendors.
insights.quote: I think people spend 5% corporations, you know, low single digits on this kind of corporate security, cyber security. I mean, I think it's got to double now.

insights.claim: Calacanis notes Bitcoin fell back to about $76-77K a week after his call that it would never reach a new all-time high, and says he would take 100K bets against Grant Cardone, Fred Krueger and others if a third-party escrow held stakes in a productive asset like the S&P 500.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: The hack added pressure to Bitcoin amid a loud public bear-bull debate; wager escrow is a possible product idea.

insights.claim: Calacanis argues Bitcoin is at most a 'restaurant' (dead) because the laser-eyes evangelism and bot armies that once pumped it have disappeared, while saying he respects Michael Saylor for not changing his tune and that Saylor may appear on the All-In interview program.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: Fading retail evangelism is the bear's core sentiment argument.

insights.claim: DoorDash is buying Instacart in a cash-and-stock deal worth about $17 billion at $65 per share, a roughly 25% premium to Instacart's October 22 close, claiming about $100 million a year in savings by merging DashPass and Instacart+ memberships.
insights.speaker: Lon Harris
insights.so_what: Consolidation in delivery accelerates as Instacart struggles against Uber, Amazon and Walmart.
insights.quote: DoorDash will pay $65 a share. It's about a 25% premium over Instacart's October 22nd closing price.

insights.claim: An anti-monopoly group says the combined company would control nearly 60% of US third-party grocery delivery, but Calacanis argues the market definition is too narrow, ignoring Amazon/Whole Foods, Walmart and HEB's own delivery.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: Broader market definitions weaken the antitrust case.
insights.quote: So, third-party grocery delivery service is like not grocery delivery.

insights.claim: Calacanis predicts the deal will go through quickly under Trump's FTC, unlike under Lina Khan, and says dealmakers are rushing because they see an 18-month window to lock in M&A.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: Expect a wave of M&A in the next 12-18 months before the political window closes.
insights.quote: Anything you see done in the next 12 months is because business people saying we got 18 months to to lock this up.

insights.claim: Calacanis, a shareholder in DoorDash, Instacart and Uber, calls the deal a complete overpay but rational for DoorDash because it trades at about 88x trailing earnings versus Instacart's roughly 25x, and says Uber was right to walk away.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: Use richly valued stock as acquisition currency; buy back undervalued stock instead.
insights.quote: When you have a high stock price, high multiple, you put your equity work. When it's lower, you don't.

insights.claim: Calacanis says Instacart is a slow-growth company, with quarterly revenue rising only from about $803 million three years ago to roughly $1 billion now and flat GAAP earnings, which is why it became the seller.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: Post-pandemic stagnant growers are acquisition targets; expect more such sales.
insights.quote: If you stop growing, you become a an acquisition target and there's going to be many many more companies like this.

insights.claim: Instacart's advertising and other revenue grew from about $243 million a quarter three years ago to $331 million last quarter, about $1.2 billion annualized and roughly 30% of revenue, and is where its profits come from.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: Retail media is the hidden profit engine in delivery platforms and a key asset for DoorDash.

themes.theme: AI build bottleneck and startup moats

insights.claim: Jake Newfield of Hermetiq argues agentic coding tools (Claude, Cursor, Codex) have made writing code no longer the bottleneck; the bottleneck is now the build process of compiling, verifying and testing.
insights.speaker: Jake Newfield
insights.so_what: Build and CI infrastructure is the next pain point and opportunity in AI-era software development.
insights.quote: The bottleneck is now the build process, which is the process of compiling, verifying, and testing code.

insights.claim: Hermetiq says a top AI lab pays it $240K to analyze over 2 million builds per day (4 billion build events), working at the Bazel RBE protocol level to become 'what Databricks did for Apache Spark'; it has raised $2.2 million and targets a $25 billion market.
insights.speaker: Jake Newfield
insights.so_what: A paying frontier-lab customer validates demand for build-data tooling.

insights.claim: Newfield says AI labs buy rather than build non-core tools for the same reason they use Databricks or Okta, because it diverts resources from building LLMs, and investors are reassured that labs pay rather than replicate it.
insights.speaker: Jake Newfield
insights.so_what: Being paid by the labs is the strongest defense against 'the labs will eat you' fears.
insights.quote: The reality is we get the wire every month

insights.claim: Calacanis says with technical moats eroding, the new startup moat is brand built on relentlessness, trust and hospitality-like customer attention, and advises founders to lead pitches with lighthouse customers.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: In AI markets, distribution and trust matter more than defensible code.
insights.quote: I think the new moat is that you're relentless and that people trust you and that would fall under brand.
